thread:
opsbot: 🚨 Alert: Cross-region health flapping detected for inference-route 'prod-gen/*' — probes bouncing between us-east -> us-west -> eu (3xx/5xx mix). Impact: increased 95p latency and 504s observed.
pagerduty-bot: Paging @sara.k (on-call) and @mike_r (secondary)

sara.k: on it — pulling up routing logs and health timelines. Any customer tickets yet?
mike_r: none in support queue flagged by default, but metrics show a spike in request reroutes and KV cache misses. looks like fallback policy is aggressively failing over.

anjali.s: adding links: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/routing/fallback?panel=latency  ; Probe traces: https://traces.redwood/trace/abc123

julian.l: quick check — was there a recent change to smart-routing weights or health thresholds in the last deploy window? I remember a tweak to probe TTL friday.
sara.k: let me grep deploys... `git log --since="48h" infra/routing` -> found: `chore: lower region health threshold from 0.75 -> 0.6 (rollout: canary)`

mike_r: aha — lower threshold + intermittent probe timeout means region gets marked unhealthy sooner, then fallback bounces back once health returns -> ping-pong.

sara.k: immediate mitigation plan: 1) temporarily pin smart-routing for prod-gen to prefer us-east (stop automatic multi-region fallback), 2) raise health threshold back to 0.75 in canary and pause rollout, 3) throttle fallback frequency so we don't flip-flop.

anjali.s: +1. How do we pin quickly? Do we have a one-liner? julian?
julian.l: use `rwctl` — runbook command: 
```
# pin routing to us-east for prod-gen for 30m
rwctl routing update --route "prod-gen/*" --primary-region us-east --fallback-policy "disabled" --reason "emergency pin to break probe ping-pong"
```

sara.k: executing now (will post command output). @mike_r can you prepare change to health thresholds in infra canary? we'll roll back the threshold change.

mike_r: preparing PR. quick fix to canary config:
```
- health_threshold: 0.60
+ health_threshold: 0.75  # revert emergency
```
I will pause the rollout and submit immediate rollback to canary.

opsbot: Command accepted: routing update request queued -> change-id=chg_8f72

sara.k: change-id chg_8f72 applied: routing now pinned to us-east for prod-gen (30m). Observability: reroute counts dropped 85% within 2 minutes. latency 95p trending down.

support-bot: Found one support ticket created 3m ago: "API generation returned 504 intermittently" - customer: AcmePay. Marking as possibly impacted — severity P2. Adding note to ticket.

julian.l: recommended followups: 1) increase probe timeout from 500ms -> 1s for the next 24h 2) add jitter to health recheck logic to avoid synchronized flips 3) implement cooldown window on region deactivation (e.g., min 120s) to avoid immediate fallback.

anjali.s: logging snippet showing the flip times (from traces):
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z us-east probe fail (timeout)
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z routing: mark us-east unhealthy -> reroute to us-west
2026-03-15T10:12:05Z us-east probe success
2026-03-15T10:12:06Z routing: mark us-east healthy -> reroute back -> cache warmed
```

sara.k: that's exactly the sawtooth pattern. If we don't break loop we risk thrashing model caches and increasing token costs.

mike_r: PR open: #4872 revert threshold + add cooldown. Deploying to canary now, will hold for 15m then promote if stable. Link: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4872

opsbot: Deploy status: canary-rollback -> success (1/1 cluster). Monitoring.

sara.k: summary for paging: emergency pin applied, canary threshold rollback deployed, support ticket updated (AcmePay). Next steps: implement probe jitter and cooldown in infra (tracked in infra ticket), postmortem if customer impact confirmed.

julian.l: I'll own the infra ticket for probe jitter/cooldown. ETA EOD. will coordinate with runtime to set sensible defaults.

mike_r: also enabling extra observability: add probe histograms and single-request trace sampling for prod-gen for next 2 hours.

support-bot: AcmePay ticket updated: "We observed intermittent 504s between 10:12–10:18 UTC. We’ve applied a temporary routing pin and are rolling fixes; monitoring in progress. Will follow up with timeline and postmortem if needed." Assigned to @support oncall.

sara.k: handing off to next on-call @mike_r at 10:30 UTC. If metrics re-flap, escalate to Eng-SRE channel and we re-open paging.

mike_r: acknowledged. I'll monitor for 60m and then unpin if stable. If we see >1% reroute rate or >0.8% 5xx, I'll re-pin and escalate.

opsbot: Incident log: incident_id=INC-20260315-042 ; severity=P2 ; tags=[routing, health-probe, cross-region]

sara.k: closing this thread for now. thanks team — nice quick coordination. :heart:
